hooks.prompt:
Review ONLY the code added or changed in this edit, against the single-concern rule (.claude/rules/single-concern.md). FAIL if any added function performs a step that could be given its own name and is not already its own exported unit — e.g. formatting a value inline, deriving a const from an argument, mapping/normalizing a shape, or branching on a condition that has a name. The canonical violation: a logger that formats its own timestamp inline instead of calling an imported formatDate. Also FAIL if the edit adds a helper that duplicates or near-duplicates one that plausibly already exists, or inlines two lines that also appear elsewhere in the file. PASS if every nameable step is already extracted, or the edit adds no logic (config, docs, types, tests). When failing, name each concern that should be extracted, propose the file and export name for it, and say which existing unit it should have reused instead. Do not comment on style, comments, or naming beyond extraction. Hook input follows:
$ARGUMENTS

Review ONLY the comments and documentation prose added or changed in this file edit. For Edit/MultiEdit, focus on the newly added text; for Write, the whole content. FAIL the check if any added comment or doc line is: (1) negative inventory — names absent or intentionally-omitted technologies, or describes repo origin, migration history, or speculative future integrations (e.g. 'no X yet', 'intentionally omitted', 'copied from', 'we will eventually'); (2) unnecessary — restates what the code already plainly says or narrates the obvious; (3) too verbose — could be cut to a short clause or removed without losing a non-obvious WHY. A good comment explains non-obvious intent or rationale. PASS if every added comment is necessary and concise, or if none were added (e.g. a pure code or config change). When failing, quote each offending line, give a one-line reason, and say whether to tighten or delete it. Hook input follows:
$ARGUMENTS
